vulnerabilities.explanation: BuilderWallet uses a two-step initialization where `builderAdmin` is set by calling `init(address)`. However, `init` has no access control (does not restrict caller to FACTORY) and no one-time guard (can be called repeatedly). Therefore, any address can set or overwrite `builderAdmin` at any time. Since `sweep()` is gated solely by `msg.sender == builderAdmin`, an attacker can seize control of any deployed BuilderWallet and steal all tokens held by it. This is directly exploitable because these wallets are intended to receive fees (via `RiskEngine` feeRecipient computation), so they may accumulate significant balances.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario:
1) Identify a builder wallet address (deterministically derived from a builderCode, or observed on-chain after `deployBuilder`).
2) Wait until the wallet has accumulated fee tokens.
3) Call `BuilderWallet.init(attackerAddress)` from any EOA/contract, overwriting the legitimate admin.
4) Call `BuilderWallet.sweep(token, attackerAddress)` to transfer the wallet’s entire token balance to the attacker.
This does not require compromising OWNER/guardian; it only requires the wallet to exist and hold tokens.

prediction.overall_explanation: The main RiskEngine contract is largely computational (view/pure) with privileged fund movement restricted to the guardian, so typical external attackers have little direct surface there. However, the BuilderWallet design contains a critical, concrete exploit: `init()` is unprotected and re-callable, allowing anyone to take over builder wallets and drain accumulated fee tokens via `sweep()`. This is a real fund-loss vulnerability affecting any fees routed to these wallets.
